scopeLede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a timber loft, a concrete tower and a restaurant. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.

scopeRows.factor: Building approval and certificate of insurance
scopeRows.why: Most managed buildings won't schedule work until they have both, and some name specific insurance limits.
Booked time windows decide when materials and crews get in, and how long a day on site really is.
Most West Loop streets have little parking near the door, so carrying tools and materials in takes time.
Wire can be fished through wood framing, has to run in conduit across concrete, or needs approved core drilling through a slab.
In a loft, conduit is part of the look. It's planned so it reads as intentional, which takes longer than hidden wiring.
Heavy chandeliers on 14-foot-plus ceilings need the right support, the right box and sometimes a lift.
Restaurants and occupied offices often need early, late or weekend work. [CONFIRM: whether after-hours rates apply]
In high-rises, fire alarm and life-safety tie-ins go through the building's own contractor.
Many unit jobs go through the City's Express Permit Program. Build-outs need plans and a standard review.
Boards often want a written proposal before they approve work in common areas or shared garages.
Whose meter the charger runs from, the building's spare capacity, and submetering decide the design.

hourlyAnswer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a West Loop job depend on everything in the table above. A fixture swap in a walk-up and the same fixture on a 16-foot loft ceiling aren't the same job. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.
choosingBuildingWhy: A loft with an exposed timber ceiling, a concrete-slab tower and a restaurant kitchen are three different jobs.
choosingBuildingAnswer: High-rise and loft units, new-construction mid-rises, tenant build-outs and a Halsted St restaurant
choosingPaperworkWhy: Most towers want a certificate of insurance, and sometimes an elevator booking, before work is scheduled.
whereWeFit: Highlights is a family-owned contractor. In the West Loop we're the right call for condo, loft and townhome work, lighting, panels, EV chargers, restaurants, tenant build-outs and mid-rise new construction. Base-building work on a 40-storey tower is a job for the large commercial firms, and we'll tell you so.

honestContext: We're a north-side shop. Most of our 1,213 Chicago permits are in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27, and the 27th covers part of the West Loop. Our West Loop work peaked with the mid-rise building wave of 2013 to 2020. Since then it has been mostly unit-level work: lighting, panels, circuits and EV chargers.
The busiest names in West Loop permits are large commercial contractors working on towers and office floors. That's a different job from yours if you're refitting a loft.

reviews.label: EV charger in a downtown condo building
reviews.text: I find that it's not easy to find good service providers in downtown Chicago, but Boz and Highlights Chicago are certainly among the best!  I needed to install a Tesla EV charger connected to my building's grid and have an submeter to track energy consumption. While others were quoting exorbitant prices or even deeming the project impossible, Boz made the discussions very straightforward and provided a reasonable quote. The team provided the required certificate of liability insurance on the same day I requested, I got the project approved by my building's association and had the installation scheduled.  The execution was on point! The team arrived at the exact time scheduled, with everything they needed and perfectly installed my charger as requested, all with proper care, safety and cleanliness. Shout out to Boz, Iva, Kaplan, Gerardo, Cristian and Matthew, a super team of super experts! I'll definitely recommend their services to others in my building and friends.

reviews.label: Panel and outlets in a high-rise unit
reviews.text: It is quite hard to find "good" contract work. It is even harder to find "good" contract work done by really nice and genuine people. Juve and Marin, two electricians from Highlights Chicago, came to complete a project at my property and they were absolutely delightful. They were respectful and aware of all of the rules that needed to be followed in high rise buildings, they were extremely patient navigating the tough parking situation, elevator challenges, and back and forth trips to bring materials and tools from their vehicles to the 4th floor unit. They spent ample time not only answering all of my questions but walking me through the process so that I was becoming educated about what was happening along the way. They did a phenomenal job with the actual electrical work, replacing a full electrical panel, several outlets in the kitchen and bathroom, and moving light fixtures. They go above and beyond what you would expect for electrical work. To add to the great experience,  Bozidar, the managing director at Highlights, was exceptional in following the progression of the project with kindness and expertise.

reviews.label: Loft with high ceilings
reviews.text: Highly recommend Highlights Chicago for any of your electrical needs.  They were very easy to work with. Boz, came by and gave a quote. Iva did all the scheduling. And Jimmy, Christobal and Davor did fabulous work.  Everyone was friendly and profesional. Can't say enough good things about the overall experience and the finished work. We are in a loft with high ceilings and they were installing large chandeliers, fans and pendant lights.

reviews.label: Downtown high-rise condo
reviews.text: I had an awesome experience using Highlights for my downtown highrise condo project. The work list included a large variety of tasks such as adding a new outlet, new ceiling fans, stove outlet, new dimmers. Everything was done on time and everything was left very clean. I was also very impressed by the efficiency of the project management team in terms of getting me a quote and refining the quote as I kept changing my mind. Finally, every technician seemed very knowledgeable and able to make good decisions on the fly, and adapt to problems on the spot. I also appreciated that they were able to guide me on decisions that had functional and aesthetic implications. For example, on the spacing for the recessed lights I wanted their opinion since they must see so many more kitchens and hallways per month than I've ever seen in my life. So they gave their honest opinion on what would look good, and I'm very happy with the results.

reviews.label: Proposal for an HOA board
reviews.text: I had an excellent experience with Highlights Chicago from start to finish. Boz came out for the initial inspection and provided a detailed, well-written proposal for my HOA board. Out of the four proposals I received, theirs was not only the most professional but also the most fairly priced.  On installation day, the team showed up early, worked efficiently, and was minimally disruptive throughout the process. The quality of work was outstanding—they left everything spotless, as if no work had ever been done, except now I have a perfectly installed EV charger.  A huge shoutout to Cristobal and Cesar for their precision and professionalism in getting the install done right the first time. Everything about this experience was smooth, transparent, and reliable. I would absolutely recommend Highlights Chicago to anyone looking for electrical work or EV charger installation.

reviews.label: Heavy fixture in a high-rise
reviews.text: I can't say enough good things about our experience with Highlights Chicago Installing a large, heavy light fixture in a tall-ceilinged room in a high-rise is no small feat, but they handled it with absolute ease, confidence, and class. From the moment they arrived, they were calm, prepared, and focused. They took every safety precaution seriously, navigated the space skillfully, and managed the entire install with quiet efficiency. The fixture was not only installed perfectly--it looks like it was always meant to be there. Their attention to detail and pride in their work really showed!

reviews.label: 17 recessed lights in a condo
reviews.text: We got several estimates to have recessed lighting put in our condo (17 in total). Not only was Highlights Chicago the best cost wise, but they were in depth with the estimate and very responsive to any questions we had prior to the project. Victor, Benjamin & Gus arrived on time, were very friendly, detailed with covering everything in plastic and did an excellent job installing our lights. We were absolutely thrilled with result and will not hesitate to recommend Highlights to our friends and family.

reviews.label: New construction
reviews.text: We simply cannot recommend Highlights Chicago highly enough. They handled all the electrical work for our new house, which is a massive job, and they were truly outstanding from start to finish. Right from the initial meeting, Boz was fantastic. He gave us a very accurate, honest assessment of exactly what our new home needed and never once tried to upsell or push unnecessary work—something we really appreciated in the middle of a big build. His estimates were delivered precisely when promised, keeping our project on schedule. The work itself was of exceptionally high quality. They wired our entire house in a timely manner, and the result is honestly outstanding. The ultimate seal of approval came from the city inspector, who actually went out of his way to compliment the new service installation, saying it was "done by the books." That kind of third-party praise speaks volumes about the quality and professionalism of their team. Boz and his crew were always professional, easy to reach, and punctual. They took the time to clarify all our questions and made sure we understood what was being done every step of the way.

faq.question: Do you work in West Loop high-rise buildings?
faq.answer: Yes. We work to the building's rules: a certificate of insurance before scheduling, booked freight elevator time, approved working hours and the building engineer's sign-off where it's needed. Reviewers describe our crews handling high-rise parking, elevators and building rules without fuss.

faq.question: Can you install an EV charger in my condo building's garage?
faq.answer: Usually, yes. The design depends on whose electrical service the charger runs from, the building's spare capacity, whether the association wants a submeter, and its approval process. We provide the certificate of insurance and a proposal the association can review.

faq.question: Do I need a permit for electrical work in my West Loop condo?
faq.answer: Most electrical work in Chicago needs a permit, and many unit jobs go through the City's Express Permit Program. Our own West Loop record includes permitted lighting work in condo units. We tell you at the walkthrough whether your job needs one, and we pull and close it.

faq.question: Do you work on restaurants on Randolph Street and in Greektown?
faq.answer: Yes: kitchen equipment circuits, service upgrades, lighting, emergency and exit lighting, and signage, scheduled around service. Our West Loop record includes a restaurant build-out on S Halsted.

faq.question: Which West Loop ZIP codes do you cover?
faq.answer: All of them: 60607, 60661 and the part of 60606 west of the river, along with every other Chicago neighbourhood.
